properties.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn), lots 4232011 and 4232012 (recorded 2022-08-30; active), split along a straight line; cross-checked against Potrero Power Station Design for Development Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
properties.digitization_method: NEWLY ADDED 2026-09-16 -- user-flagged that this feature, though already referenced in this dataset's own text (an earlier Block 3 note calls it 'a separate, physically distant open space between Blocks 15 and 7'), was never actually digitized as its own tracked polygon. Figure 6.2.3 labels 'LOUISIANA PASEO' directly as a landscaped pedestrian path running the full north-south length between Block 15 (west) and Blocks 7/11 (east), from Humboldt Street down to 23rd Street, opening into Power Station Park where Block 7 ends. Built here as a 6-vertex polygon using this project's own already-committed, GDAL/TPS-corrected corners for Block 15's east edge and Block 7/Block 11's west edges directly (not independently re-measured), so it shares an exact boundary with all three blocks by construction -- zero gap, zero overlap -- and its south end sits flush with Power Station Park's own west edge (also built from Block 11's same NW corner), so the two connect exactly as the diagram shows. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the source URL cited for this file (the August 22, 2019 public-review draft #2 of the D4D, dead with a 404) is replaced by the final D4D (February 26, 2020), where Figure 6.2.3 Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247) labels 'LOUISIANA PASEO' between Block 15 and Blocks 7/11, with Humboldt Street above, 23rd Street below and Power Station Park beside Blocks 7 and 11. Correction to the text above: the figure's label does not say 'landscaped'; D4D Section 4.25 describes the paseo as providing 'flexible-use urban plaza spaces and car-free pedestrian areas', and its enlargement concept plan is Figure 4.30.1. The committed geometry was not changed. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- a simplified straight-sided approximation of a car-free pedestrian paseo; the final D4D's enlargement concept plan (Figure 4.30.1) shows it as a non-rectangular space with planting and plaza areas not captured here. Positional accuracy matches whatever the adjoining Block 15/7/11 files currently carry (see their own accuracy_caveat) since this polygon is built directly from their vertices.'. REPLACED 2026-10-10 (shape; status and use unchanged): the owner read Assessor lots 4232011 and 4232012 as Louisiana Paseo and Power Station Park together, with 4232011 split between the paseo strip (continuing lot 4232012) and the park arm at right angles to it. The recorded east-edge vertices of both lots lie within 0.1 m of one straight line, which is used as the cut through 4232011 (about 33 m, not a recorded lot line). The outline is now lot 4232012 plus the west strip of lot 4232011 (2,395 m2), in place of the earlier 2,642 m2 shape. geometry_type stays 'approximate' because of the cut. The earlier sign-off covered the earlier shape; this change was made at the owner's direction. CLEANED 2026-10-11 (two duplicate vertices removed; no change to the shape, status or use): the outline had the same point twice at its start (an exact repeat of the corner at about 37.756040, -122.384551) and two points 0.06 m apart on the east edge of the strip (-122.384396436 and -122.384395842, 37.75634). The first of each pair was dropped, leaving the vertex that Power Station Park also uses. Area changes by under 0.1 m2. 2026-10-11: text only. Public text that said the lots were 'assigned by the owner' now says they are Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams, because readers would take 'owner' to mean the landowner. No change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- the outline is built from recorded Assessor lot lines except one cut. The two lots are Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams: Louisiana Paseo is the north-south strip made of lot 4232012 and the west strip of lot 4232011, and Power Station Park is the east-west arm of lot 4232011. The line between them, about 33 m long through lot 4232011, is not a recorded lot line: it is the straight extension of the strip's east edge, which the recorded vertices of both lots lie on to within 0.1 m. The paseo is planned: design review approved (annual reports: 8/3/21; memo June 2022) and no construction reported as of the March 2025 annual report.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Louisiana Paseo is the strip made of Assessor lot 4232012 and the west strip of lot 4232011 (both active, recorded 2022-08-30), assigned from Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams; no document names these lots as the paseo, and the line through lot 4232011 is a straight extension, not a recorded lot line.
properties.regulatory_context: A car-free, flexible-use pedestrian paseo and plaza space (D4D Sections 4.25 and 4.30), labelled 'LOUISIANA PASEO' on the final D4D's Figure 6.2.3 and running from Humboldt Street to 23rd Street between Block 15 and Blocks 7/11, opening into Power Station Park.
properties.notes: Louisiana Paseo of the Potrero Power Station Design for Development, shown as part of Assessor lots 4232011 and 4232012 (see the accuracy note). Newly added 2026-09-16; previously mentioned only in passing in other blocks' notes, never tracked as its own feature. Status 'planned': design review approved (annual reports: 8/3/21; memo June 2022) and no construction reported as of the March 2025 annual report. Use 'park': the final D4D treats it as open space (Section 4.25).
